title: Why It Still Matters: Napoleon's legacy

segments.text: Napoleon lost at Waterloo, but we still live in his world.
His civil code made all citizens equal before the law,
and it shaped legal systems from Europe to Latin America.
He swept away feudal privilege across half a continent.
His invasions taught people to think of themselves as nations,
and that idea built Germany and Italy.
After he fell, the great powers met in Vienna, to keep Europe in balance.
That balance held for about forty years, and then began to crack.
A united Germany upset it, and rival alliances formed in response.
In nineteen fourteen, those alliances turned one shot into a world war.
The man who redrew Europe is still redrawing how we live.
